meta.title: Operational details in an Epic EHI export
meta.subtitle: The scheduling, rooming-adjacent, and workflow exhaust most clinical exports leave behind.

summary: This export does not expose a clean exam-room timer for ordinary office visits. It does expose the visit choreography: scheduled slots, check-in/check-out actors, first vitals timestamps, AVS print times, eCheck-in steps, questionnaire attempts, order timing, and audit events.

The strongest finding is the audit/workflow layer. There are thousands of timestamped record-change events and multiple patient-facing workflow ledgers, which is far beyond a normal clinical summary export.

surfaceRows.label: Appointment slot
surfaceRows.interpretation: Booked wall-clock appointment time. This is often absent from standard clinical exports.

surfaceRows.label: Check-in actor
surfaceRows.interpretation: The staff or MyChart account that checked the appointment in.

surfaceRows.label: Check-out actor
surfaceRows.interpretation: Checkout exists mostly for office visits; labs/radiology often have no checkout row.

surfaceRows.label: eCheck-in workflow
surfaceRows.interpretation: Rollup status plus per-step rows for insurance, questionnaires, travel history, payments, and more.

surfaceRows.label: Flowsheet timing
surfaceRows.interpretation: A timestamped proxy for rooming/vitals when vitals or screening rows were charted.

surfaceRows.label: Room or bed assignment
surfaceRows.interpretation: The columns exist, but this outpatient-heavy specimen does not carry room/bed values.

surfaceRows.label: ADT in/out events
surfaceRows.interpretation: Four events reconstruct two outpatient therapy-series contacts: in events by a user, discharge events by a batch job.

surfaceRows.label: Video visit sidecar
surfaceRows.interpretation: The table is populated as a 1:1 sidecar, but video-visit values are empty here.

sections.title: Not a room timer, but close enough to see workflow

narrative.text: The ordinary office-visit rows do not contain a clean 'roomed at' and 'left exam room at' pair. Instead, the strongest rooming proxy is the first same-visit flowsheet timestamp, usually vitals or screening, compared with the scheduled slot time.

For clinic visits with such a proxy, the first core vital can land before the slot, at the slot, or later; that variability is itself useful because it shows why an EHI export should be read as operational evidence, not a stopwatch.

sections.title: The record has an audit trail

narrative.text: The largest operational layer is not a visit table at all. Patient-record and hospital-account audit views expose timestamped changes, changed-item labels, and users. This dive uses counts and item categories, not raw old/new values.

sections.title: The front desk is in the record

narrative.text: A standard clinical export would usually say the visit happened. This EHI export says when it was scheduled, whether it was completed or canceled, who checked it in, whether it was checked out, and whether an AVS was printed.
The appointment skeleton also has false positives: many encounters have appointment sidecar rows, but the real scheduled appointments are the rows with status and slot time.

sections.title: Patient work before the visit is structured

narrative.text: The eCheck-in and questionnaire layer breaks patient-facing previsit work into step rows, form assignments, attempt statuses, and even seconds spent in questionnaire workflow. It is not a note; it is a workflow ledger.

Orders carry more than clinical intent. Labs and imaging include order time, procedure begin/start/end fields, result time, and occasionally charge-drop time. The sidecar table named for first/last scheduling exists here, but its timestamps are blank.

The note lifecycle tables expose local entry, file, and update-by-author times. In this specimen, true local filing is mostly business-hours work, with a smaller after-hours tail and no weekend filing signal.

sections.title: ADT machinery appears even in outpatient therapy

narrative.text: The ADT event trail is present for two therapy-series contacts. It records an outpatient in event by a named user and a discharge event filed later by a Prelude batch job. That is operationally rich, but not the same thing as time spent with a clinician.

e_slot_vitals_proxy.text: Real scheduled appointments are identified by PAT_ENC.APPT_STATUS_C_NAME / PAT_ENC_APPT.PROV_START_TIME. Flowsheet RECORDED_TIME gives a rooming-adjacent proxy on 12 of 23 status-bearing appointments.

e_no_exam_room_timer.text: A schema search found room/arrival/departure columns in CLARITY_ADT and PAT_ENC_HSP, but ordinary internal-medicine appointments in this specimen have no exported room-in/room-out timestamp pair.

e_appt_status_counts.text: Status-bearing appointments total 23: 19 Completed, 3 Canceled, 1 Scheduled. Completed appointments all have check-in users; checkout appears on 10 rows.

e_skeleton_filter.text: PAT_ENC_APPT has 74 rows, but only 23 carry appointment status and 23 carry slot time. Use status or slot time to identify real scheduled appointments.

e_echeckin_steps.text: ECHKIN_STEP_INFO contains 144 step rows across appointment eCheck-in workflows, with rollup statuses in PAT_ENC_4.ECHKIN_STATUS_C_NAME.

e_questionnaire_workflow.text: Questionnaire-related tables add 20 MyChart appointment questionnaire rows, 20 kiosk questionnaire rows, and 10 CL_QANSWER rows with workflow duration values ranging from 4 to 72 seconds.

e_audit_trail.text: V_EHI_REG_ITEM_AUDIT_EPT has 6477 patient-record audit rows across 12 changed-item labels. V_EHI_REG_ITEM_AUDIT_HAR adds 42 hospital-account audit rows across 13 labels.

e_order_timing.text: ORDER_PROC has 42 orders; all have ORDER_TIME, 36 have procedure timing fields, and 20 have RESULT_TIME. CL_ORD_FST_LST_SCH has 62 rows but no populated first/last scheduled timestamps.

e_note_timing.text: Clinical note lifecycle rows include 82 local entry instants, 80 local note-file instants, and 82 local update-by-author instants. Local note-file times show 7 after-hours rows and 0 weekend rows. All 7 after-hours filed notes with slots were same-day: 2 from morning slots, 4 from afternoon slots, and 1 from late-day slots.

e_adt_therapy.text: CLARITY_ADT has four events for two MHM OT Neuro Central therapy-series contacts: Hospital Outpatient in-events by a named user and Discharge out-events filed by PRELUDE, BATCH JOB. PAT_ENC_HSP has 2 therapy-series rows with admission/discharge times but no ED arrival, triage, ED departure, room, or bed values.
